dublinCore.title: Interactive Spectrogram Parameter Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Spectrogram
Short-time Fourier transform
Time-frequency analysis
Window functions
Zero padding
Signal processing
dublinCore.description: Two spectrograms of the same signal (a synthetic chirp, two close tones, a strong and a weak tone, tone bursts, a vibrato whistle, or the live microphone), each computed with its own window length, overlap, window type, zero-padding factor, dB floor and color map. Guided challenges load contrasting settings with a prediction prompt and a Reveal button; a linked cursor reports time, frequency and level in both panels, and a slice plot compares the two frame spectra under it.
relation: Chapter 14: Time-Frequency Analysis and Advanced Topics

searchKeywords: zero padding does not improve resolution

topic: Display dynamic range and color maps
learningObjectives: Calculate the time span N/fs, frequency resolution fs/N, hop size, frames per second and number of frames of an STFT from its window length, overlap and sampling rate
Analyze why neither a very short nor a very long window draws a chirp as a thin line, using the sweep during one window
Distinguish true frequency resolution (fs/N) from the FFT bin spacing produced by zero padding (fs/(PN))
Explain how overlap and window shape affect what a spectrogram shows (missed bursts, spectral leakage) without changing N/fs or fs/N
Evaluate a set of spectrogram parameters (window, length, overlap, dB floor, color map) for a given signal and justify the choice

misconceptions.correction: Zero padding samples the spectrum of the same window more densely; the main-lobe width, and so the resolution, is set by the window length N
misconceptions.evidence: Challenge 3: A (N = 128, pad x8, 1024-point FFT) shows one peak about 130 Hz wide for tones 60 Hz apart, while B (N = 1024) separates them with a 56 dB dip

misconceptions.misconception: More overlap gives a sharper spectrogram
misconceptions.correction: Overlap only samples time more densely; N/fs and fs/N do not change
misconceptions.evidence: Challenge 4: both captions show 32 ms and 31.25 Hz; with 0% overlap the bursts peak between -10.1 and -36.0 dB, with 75% between -10.1 and -11.3 dB

misconceptions.misconception: A longer window always draws a sharper line
misconceptions.correction: A frequency that changes during the window is smeared over the range it sweeps
misconceptions.evidence: Challenge 1: at t = 1 s the chirp is about 60 Hz wide with N = 256 but about 230 Hz wide with N = 2048

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Two spectrograms of the same signal, A above B, each computed with its own window length, overlap, window type, zero padding, dB floor and color map. A drop-down chooses a synthetic signal or the live microphone, guided challenges load contrasting settings with a prediction and a Reveal button, and pointing at a spectrogram shows the time, frequency and level in both panels and compares the two frame spectra in a slice plot.

colorScheme.spectrogram: viridis, inferno, gray or jet color map

controls.label: Signal
controls.description: Chooses the analyzed signal: chirp, two close tones, strong + weak tone, tone bursts, vibrato whistle or the live microphone

controls.label: Challenge
controls.description: Loads one of nine guided challenges (settings for A and B, signal, cursor and zoom) with a prediction prompt

options.label: 1. Short vs long window on a chirp
2. Two close tones: who separates them?
3. Zero padding vs a longer window
5. Rectangular vs Hann: a weak tone

controls.label: Reveal / Hide
controls.description: Shows or hides the answer to the current challenge (disabled in free exploration)

controls.label: Start mic / Stop mic
controls.description: Switches to the microphone and opens it (analyzed only, never played through the speakers); Stop releases it and freezes the spectrograms

controls.label: Zoom
controls.description: Magnifies the frequency axis of both spectrograms; clicking a spectrogram centers the zoom

controls.label: Edit: A / B
controls.description: Narrow screens only: chooses which panel's controls are shown

controls.label: Window N (A)
controls.description: Window length of panel A: 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 or 2048 samples

controls.label: Overlap (A)
controls.description: Overlap of successive frames of panel A: 0, 25, 50, 75, 87.5 or 93.75 percent (hop H = N, 3N/4, N/2, N/4, N/8, N/16)

controls.label: dB floor (A)
controls.description: Level drawn with the lowest color in panel A; display only

controls.label: Zero padding (A)
controls.description: FFT length P x N for panel A

controls.label: Window N (B)
controls.description: Window length of panel B: 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 or 2048 samples

controls.label: Overlap (B)
controls.description: Overlap of successive frames of panel B: 0, 25, 50, 75, 87.5 or 93.75 percent

controls.label: dB floor (B)
controls.description: Level drawn with the lowest color in panel B; display only

controls.label: Zero padding (B)
controls.description: FFT length P x N for panel B

visualElements.description: Spectrogram A and spectrogram B (time across, frequency up, level as color), with a linked cursor, the analysis window of the frame under it, and a rug of frame centers
Slice plot: the A and B frame spectra under the cursor over a 1000 Hz span, with dots on bins fs/N apart
Per-panel read-outs N/fs, fs/N (and FFT bin spacing), frames per second and number of frames; cursor time, frequency and level in A and B; challenge prompt or answer

model.description: Short-time Fourier transform of a 2 s signal at 8000 Hz (synthetic) or of the live microphone, low-pass filtered and decimated to about 8 kHz; two independent parameter sets; levels in dB relative to a sinusoid of amplitude 1
equations: X[m,k] = sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x[n + mH] w[n] e^{-j 2 pi k n / (P N)}
number of frames = floor((L - N) / H) + 1
algorithms: Periodic Hann, Hamming, Blackman and rectangular windows
Sample stitching of overlapping p5.FFT.waveform() blocks
Peak-preserving rendering (each pixel shows the strongest STFT cell it covers)

instructionalStrategies: Predict, then reveal, for each guided challenge
Contrast two parameter sets on the same signal
Verify read-outs against hand calculations of N/fs, fs/N and frame counts
extensions: Add a Gaussian or Kaiser window
Load a recorded speech or music file as a source
